en: The Twenty-One Homages to Noble Tārā. Om! Homage to the Blessed One, the Noble and Glorious Twenty-One Tārā!
Homage to you, O Tārā, O Swift One, O Heroine, whose eyes resemble the flash of lightning!
O you who are born from the blossoming lotus-like mouth of the Lord of the Three Worlds!
Homage to you, O lady of beautiful countenance, who are like the full moon of a hundred autumns,
blazing with rays that shine more brightly than the light of a thousand stars.
Homage to her who is adorned with lotus-like hands bearing golden and blue lotuses;
whose sphere of activity consists of generosity, heroism, austerity, self-restraint, patience, and meditative concentration.
Homage to the Tathāgata-Uṣṇīṣa-Vijayā, whose conduct is infinite, who is served by the sons of the Victors who have attained the remaining perfections. || 4 ||
Homage to her who fills the quarters and the reaches of space with the syllables *Tāra* and *Huṃ*, who has stepped across the seven worlds, and whose gaze is filled with infinite compassion. (5)
Homage to her who is worshipped by Śakra, Agni, Brahmā, the Maruts, and the Lord of the Viśvedevas;
she who is preceded by hosts of spirits, vetālas, gandharvas, and yakṣas.
Homage to her who, with the sound "phaṭ," crushes the supreme *yantra*;
she whose foot is set in the *pratyālīḍha* stance, the one with the crest of flames.
Blazing and radiant with a mass of flames.
Homage to Namasturā, the Great Terrible One, the destroyer of the heroes of Mālava, whose lotus-face is knit with a frown, the slayer of all enemies! 8.
Homage to her whose heart is adorned with fingers marked by the seal of the jewel of women,
and who fills the entire circle of the quarters with the multitude of her own hands.
Homage to her who spreads forth a stream of milk from pearls, all of them exceedingly joyful;
to Tārā, who laughs and laughs aloud, and who brings under her control the fickle Māra.
Homage to her who draws in the hosts of all kings with a single glance,
who releases one from all calamities with her frowning brow and the syllable *hūṃ*. 11.
Homage to her who is radiant with ornaments of jasmine and moon-fragments, who shines with the mass of light conquered by Amitābha, and who is preeminent in her rays. 12.
Homage to her who stands amidst the garlands of flames of the fire at the end of the aeon, who,
with a joyful stance in the *ālīḍha* posture,
utterly destroys the entire circle of enemies.
Homage to her who strikes the ground with her feet, clapping them with her hands.
With a frown and the utterance of the syllable Hūṃ, she pierces through the seven netherworlds.
Homage to you, O auspicious Śivā, peaceful one, whose sphere is tranquil nirvāṇa;
you who are joined with the *svāhā* and the *praṇava*, and who destroy great sins. 15.
Homage to her who shatters the bodies of enemies bound by pride,
who is illumined by the syllable *hūṃ* of the Vidyā-mantra, and who is established in the placement of the ten-syllable words.
Homage to Tārā, who is stirred by the *huṃ* syllable and the stamping of her feet;
she who moves through Mount Meru, Maṇḍala, Kailāsa, and the three worlds. (17)
Homage to the one who abides upon the moon held in the hand,
and whose *phaṭ* syllable is uttered twice with the color of green.
The destroyer of all poisons without exception. || 18 ||
Homage to her who is served by the hosts of gods, asuras, yakṣas, and kinnaras;
she who brings about the unawakened joy and enjoyment, and who destroys evil dreams. 19.
Salutations to her who shines with the brilliance of eyes fully like the moon and sun;
to her whose *tuttāre* is uttered by the stars; to the destroyer of unevenly blazing [afflictions].
Homage to the one who is the arrangement of the female principle, endowed with Śiva and Śakti;
to the supreme and swift one who destroys planets, vetālas, yakṣas, and fevers.
This hymn, the "Twenty-One Homages," has the mantra as its root.
The wise person who, endowed with devotion to the Goddess, recites it in the morning while remaining self-restrained, [attains success]. (22)
Having risen either in the evening or in the morning, one should remember that which bestows fearlessness upon all, which pacifies all sins, and which destroys all miserable rebirths. (23)
He shall quickly be consecrated by seven crores of Victors;
and within just one month, he shall happily proceed to the state of Buddhahood. || 24 ||
Whether it be his most terrible poison, whether stationary or mobile, it does not take effect upon mere remembrance, even if it has been swallowed or drunk. (25)
It destroys the poison of others' wives for those afflicted by the poison of the net of planetary influences, as well as for other sentient beings; it is effective when recited fourteen times.
One desiring a son shall obtain a son; one desiring wealth shall obtain wealth;
one obtains all desires and is not thwarted by obstacles. (27)
Thus concludes the One Hundred and Eight Names of the Noble Goddess Tārā, spoken by the Blessed One, the Glorious Samyaksaṃbuddha Vairocana, as uttered by the Buddha.
